headline: 英國藝廊與冰島新片
context: 英國皇家藝術學院（Royal Academy）推出畫家 Richard Dadd 回顧展，他19世紀曾因殺害父親被關進 Bedlam 精神病院，卻也在那裡畫出許多奇幻而知名的仙靈題材作品。同時，冰島背景的災難愛情片《The Fires》也上映，描述火山學家對抗一波接一波的火山噴發危機。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Royal Academy, London Dadd was already a remarkable artist – with fairies as his hit theme – before he was locked up for murder. Yet it was within the confines of Bedlam that he saw nature and art afresh The young man in the garden must be one of Richard Dadd’s fellow patients in Bedlam, you think. His unkempt hair and ruffled clothes are sure indications of a distracted mind as he sits, half his face in shadow, hands nervously clasped, on a fabulously twisted wooden bench surrounded by greenery that’s almost too lush for comfort. Yet the subject of Dadd’s 1853 Portrait of a Young Man is probably the superintendent of Bethlem Hospital, Dr Charles Hood. The painter sees reflections of his own mental state in this frail-seeming young clinician. Patient and doctor are not so different, he suggests. There is the finest of lines between “sanity” and “madness”. Dadd crossed that line when he murdered his father whom he thought was the devil, then tried to kill a stranger while fleeing to Paris. He was quickly caught and would spend the rest of his life in Bedlam and Broadmoor. But how much does his mental illness explain his arresting, bizarre, sometimes unforgettable images? Is he a kind of Victorian acid casualty whose visions of fairies are the peculiar fruit of his psychosis? Continue reading...
sources.title: Richard Dadd review – can his mental illness help explain these arresting, bizarre images?

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: A volcanologist and a photographer try to save Reykjavik in impressive and plausible drama This scientifically plausible, CGI-tastic disaster film will either do wonders for Iceland’s tourist industry or destroy it completely. Vigdís Hrefna Pálsdóttir stars as a volcanologist called Anna, who is descended from a short line of volcanologists (just her dad). When mini volcanos start erupting and earthquakes get more frequent, Anna begins to suspect the subterranean systems everyone thought were separate might all be fed from one big magma lake deep underground. Great gaseous clouds of geologic mumbo jumbo get spewed into the dialogue, backed up with sombre graphs on computer screens and people drawing stuff on blackboards. But the gist is that Reykjavik is in danger. Of course, the powers that be are sceptical about Anna’s theories and don’t want to cut off the island’s supply of sweet, sweet tourist money. Pretty soon, though, the signs are too numerous to ignore. And a big eruption either could last a day or two, or as Anna points out, for 30 years, like a volcano that erupted in the 9th century. (Good thing Icelandic history goes back that far.) Continue reading...
sources.title: The Fires review – volcanoes and passions erupt in Iceland disaster-romance

threads_text:
英國藝廊與冰島新片

英國皇家藝術學院（Royal Academy）正在展出畫家 Richard Dadd 的回顧展。他19世紀時因殺害自己的父親被關進 Bedlam 精神病院度過餘生，卻也在那段期間畫出許多奇幻、詭異又教人印象深刻的仙靈題材作品，評論認為他的精神狀態或許正是這些畫作獨特之處的來源之一。

電影這邊，以冰島雷克雅維克（Reykjavik）為背景的災難愛情片《The Fires》也上映了。女主角是一位火山學家，發現原本被認為各自獨立的地底火山系統，其實可能都連接同一個巨大岩漿湖，雷克雅維克因此面臨隨時可能爆發的危機。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 7 月 21 日發佈的報導。
voice_text: 今天藝文圈有兩則新鮮事，一個在畫廊，一個在戲院。先說畫展，英國皇家藝術學院在辦一位19世紀畫家的回顧展，他年輕時殺了自己的父親，被關進精神病院度過餘生，卻也是在那段時間，畫出許多奇幻詭異的仙靈題材作品。電影這邊，有一部以冰島為背景的災難愛情片上映，女主角是位火山學家，發現當地好幾座火山其實共用同一個地底岩漿湖，整座城市都面臨爆發危機。
